heading: INT. TELEGRAPH OFFICE - GRAND CENTRAL JUNCTION - 1912 - DAWN

units.text: INT. TELEGRAPH OFFICE - GRAND CENTRAL JUNCTION - 1912 - DAWN
A brass-and-mahogany room that smells of oil and coal.
The sounder clicks like a nervous insect.
Pale light slants through a high window onto a counter and a wall of pigeonholes.
HOBSON, 50, the night operator, sleeves gartered, bends over the key with a steady hand.
He has not looked up in an hour.
MISS ALTHEA PIKE, 30, in a gray traveling suit, stands at the counter, gloved fingers drumming a slow rhythm on the wood.
COLONEL ROWE, 60, a moustache like a broom, stands behind her with a cane planted between his boots.
The sounder stops.
Hobson tears a slip from the tape and holds it a long moment.
It says the ship has gone down.
units.name: HOBSON

units.text: Read it again.
units.name: ALTHEA

units.text: Miss Pike.
units.name: HOBSON

units.text: Colonel Rowe and Althea reach for the slip together.
Their fingers meet on the paper.
Neither lets go.
Neither speaks.
The tape between them trembles.
Give it to me, girl.
units.name: ROWE

units.text: It's my brother's name on it, Colonel.
units.name: ALTHEA

units.text: They tug.
The paper tears down the middle.
Each holds half, and each stares at the half they hold.
Behind the counter, Hobson rises very slowly and takes off his eyeshade.
There is a second line, if you will let me read it.
units.name: HOBSON

units.text: They freeze.
The sounder begins to click again.
